summary.intent: Execute Phase 27 of the cipher-box project to implement a writable shares proof-of-concept, covering the full stack from API backend through owner/recipient UI and verification.
summary.outcome: Phase 27 shipped with all 3 plans complete, 12 security fixes applied (TDD), 21 E2E tests passing, a PR created and all 23 reviewer threads resolved across 4 review rounds.

repo: cipher-box uses IPNS for file metadata records; each file requires a per-file IPNS keypair — uploads via shared folders were missing this, causing files to be unreadable after upload

ECIES key wrapping must target the correct recipient's public key; shared uploads initially wrapped the IPNS private key with the owner's key instead of the recipient's, making the recipient unable to update files
Owner file updates via useFileOperations did not re-wrap the new file key for share recipients — a pre-existing gap that only became visible when write shares were added
The share_keys table stores per-recipient encrypted keys by keyType ('file', 'folder', 'file-ipns'); a new 'file-ipns' type was needed for recipient IPNS key access
Downgrading a share must delete file-ipns entries from share_keys to prevent continued metadata modification; this requires a DB transaction wrapping both the share update and key deletion
createShare lacked a permission/IPNS-key invariant: a write share without encryptedIpnsKey or a read share with one could be created; guard added at service layer
orval (OpenAPI client generator) generates an object union type for nullable string fields instead of `string | null` — this is a known orval limitation, not a spec error
FolderIpns ownership lookup must use the sharer's userId, not the calling user's, when a write-share recipient publishes to the shared folder's IPNS record
React types (React.DragEvent etc.) referenced without import — works due to `jsx: react-jsx` tsconfig but flagged by linter; explicit import preferred
The GSD execute-phase workflow uses VERIFICATION.md and STATE.md that are sometimes created by subagents but not auto-staged by the orchestrator — they need explicit commit steps

code.finding: withConflictRetry closures captured stale React state for folderChildren and currentSequenceNumber; refs must be maintained alongside state and synced in all navigation functions (navigateToSubfolder, navigateUp, navigateToBreadcrumb, refreshFolderContents)
Original shared upload set fileMetaIpnsName to empty string; the full IPNS keypair generation must be inlined to create proper per-file records for shared uploads
Subfolder creation was wrapping keys with recipient's public key; must wrap with owner's key for FilePointer.ipnsPrivateKeyEncrypted and add a separate share_key entry for the recipient
Save path used owner-only updateFile hook; requires onSaveSharedFile callback prop passed from SharedFileBrowser to route saves through the shared navigation's update path
addShareKeys must restrict write-share recipients to 'file' and 'file-ipns' key types only — folder key injection must be blocked
Permission downgrade (encryptedIpnsKey = null + delete file-ipns share_keys) must be wrapped in a transaction to prevent partial state
After injecting SharesService into IpnsService for write-share authorization, the unit test module must provide a mock SharesService or the test suite fails with Nest DI resolution error
ECIES ciphertext hex fields need both MinLength(64) and a Matches(/^([0-9a-f]{2})+$/i) even-length hex regex — MinLength alone allows odd-length strings that fail hex decoding
upgradingId/downgradingId state can get stuck if the handler throws before reaching the finally block; entire handler body must be wrapped in try/finally to guarantee cleanup

workflow: Dev servers in Claude Code background tasks are killed when the conversation context shifts; use nohup or detach with & disown to keep them alive across conversation events
SDK packages (core, sdk-core, sdk) must be built before the web dev server can resolve @cipherbox/sdk — build order: core → sdk-core → sdk
API client (orval) must be regenerated and committed after every DTO change; missing regeneration is a common CI failure cause
Generated OpenAPI JSON files may lack a trailing newline — CI diffs will flag this; add with printf or echo >> after generation
TDD for security fixes: stash partial fixes, write failing tests against unfixed code to confirm red phase, pop stash and verify green
Security review before merge caught 12 issues (2 critical) in a single-phase feature — running /security:review after crypto-heavy phases is high value
The /simplify parallel agent review caught a critical bug: navigation functions were not syncing state refs, causing stale data after navigation
When removing tests, always check if the test was the only consumer of an imported symbol to avoid unused-import lint failures in CI
Copying .env files from the canonical checkout (cipher-box/) to debug checkouts (cipher-box-ci-debug/) is the reliable setup step for dev environment parity

friction: PostgreSQL host IP changed mid-session (192.168.133.114 → 192.168.133.12); no .env existed in the debug checkout, requiring manual creation from .env.example
Web app defaulted to window.location.origin + '/api' when VITE_API_URL was unset, connecting to port 5173 instead of 3000 — not obvious from the codebase
Background tasks repeatedly killed by conversation context shifts, requiring multiple restarts before switching to detached processes
Git lock file blocked commit after a prior interrupted operation
orval regeneration is fragile: requires the API server to be running with latest code for OpenAPI spec to reflect DTO changes, and sometimes produces stale output
VERIFICATION.md and tee-worker/package-lock.json were left uncommitted after the phase completed — caught by the user, not the workflow
CI lint failure from unused ForbiddenException import left behind when a test was removed
CI failure from missing trailing newline in generated openapi.json file — subtle diff that only shows up in CI
Four rounds of PR review resolution required due to CodeRabbit flagging issues introduced in prior fix rounds
open_items: orval nullable string type limitation: encryptedIpnsKey in ReceivedShareResponseDto generates as a union object type instead of `string | null` — accepted as PoC limitation, consumers handle it correctly
Polling fetches all received shares every 30s instead of a single-share endpoint — a dedicated endpoint would be more efficient but requires new API work beyond PoC scope

reWrapForRecipients in useFileOperations does not re-wrap file-ipns keys when the owner edits a file — by design for PoC (recipient's IPNS key is their own), but creates a gap if the owner needs to rotate keys

TextEditorDialog falls back to an explicit error for files without a share_key (H-02 fix) — pre-existing owner-uploaded files in shared folders before the fix will be unreadable by recipients and require re-upload
100-share poll limit in the periodic permission check — acceptable for PoC but needs pagination for production
E2E tests for silent revocation (30s polling detects permission change) and the full upgrade→downgrade cycle are present but depend on timing; may be flaky under slow CI
